physical_harm: No injuries or death caused, the deceased committed suicide
number_of_offences: Charges framed under s. 306 IPC, but no offence was made out
key_evidence_accepted: The Supreme Court accepted the suicide note and the SMS sent by the deceased to his brother as indicative of his intent and the absence of any direct instigation or abetment by the accused.
witness_credibility: The court assessed that there was no independent witness to the actual incident, and the complaint was found to have embellishments.
bail_history: Bail granted by the High Court on 06.8.2008

legal_representation.accused: P. S. Patwalia, Sr. Adv., Sudarshan Rajan, Mahesh Kumar, Hitain Bajaj, Rohit Bhardwaj, Saksham Maheshwari, Jagjit Singh Chhabra, Manoj Rajpoot, Advs.
legal_representation.state: Ms. Rooh-E-Hina Dua, Harshit K., Prem Malhotra, Advs.

investigation_status: Charge sheet filed on 13.9.2008, charges framed on 16.4.2009

appeal_history.supreme_court: Appeals allowed, order setting aside charges

prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the accused teachers, Head of the Department, and Principal were responsible for the suicide of the student due to their disciplinary actions, and that an FIR was registered under Section 306 of the Indian Penal Code (IPC) against them.
defence_argument: The defence argued that the disciplinary actions taken by the accused were legitimate and necessary for maintaining order in the educational institution, and that there was no evidence of abetment of suicide. They also emphasized that the suicide note indicated the deceased's own intent and that the father's anguish should not be converted into a case of abetment.
legal_principle_applied: The Supreme Court applied the legal principle that abetment of suicide requires a clear mens rea and an active act or direct act that led the deceased to commit suicide, as per the definition under Section 107 of the IPC.
precedent_relied_upon: S. S. Chheena Vs. Vijay Kumar Mahajan and Anr. (2010) 12 SCC 190; Sanju Alias Sanjay Singh Sengar Vs. State of M.P. 2002 (5) SCC 371; State of West Bengal Vs. Indrajit Kundu and Ors. 2019 (10) SCC 188; Ramesh Kumar Vs. State of Chhattisgarh (2001) 9 SCC 618
